details:
=== CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===
- scripts/lint_pr_body_auto_close.py:74-81 | severity=high | confidence=5
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, minimax_minimax-m2_5, moonshotai_kimi-k2_5, x-ai_grok-4_20]
  PROBLEM: AUTO_CLOSE_RE still allows an optional colon before the issue reference, so colon-form keywords are matched as auto-close triggers.
  WHY: GitHub does not treat colon-form keywords as auto-close triggers, so the required lint will falsely block clean PR bodies that mention examples like `Closes: #2734`.
- .github/workflows/lint-pr-body-auto-close.yml:53-74 | severity=high | confidence=5
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m2_5, moonshotai_kimi-k2_5, x-ai_grok-4_20]
  PROBLEM: The workflow only lints the PR body and never includes the PR title.
  WHY: On squash merge, an auto-close keyword in the title still reaches the merge commit, so a body-only check can pass while the issue is auto-closed.
- tests/test_lint_pr_body_auto_close.py:74-104 | severity=medium | confidence=5
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, minimax_minimax-m2_5, moonshotai_kimi-k2_5]
  PROBLEM: The positive cases still treat colon-form references as valid matches, pinning the overmatching behavior.
  WHY: These tests will keep the suite green while the regex remains wrong and will fail once the intended whitespace-only tightening is applied.
- tests/test_lint_pr_body_auto_close.py:68-115 | severity=medium | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, moonshotai_kimi-k2_5]
  PROBLEM: The test suite lacks negative coverage asserting that colon-form references should not match.
  WHY: Without explicit negatives, a future regression that reintroduces colon-form matching would not be caught.
- scripts/lint_pr_body_auto_close.py:commit b542c257 | severity=medium | confidence=5
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro]
  PROBLEM: The commit message says the workflow, regex, and tests were fixed, but the diff does not implement those changes.
  WHY: It creates a false audit trail that says the PR-title bypass and colon-overmatch gaps are closed when they are not.
- scripts/lint_pr_body_auto_close.py:248-256 | severity=low | confidence=2
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro]
  PROBLEM: Cached `None` lookup results cause the same gh failure to be appended to `lookup_errors` repeatedly for duplicate references.
  WHY: The cache skips re-fetching but still emits duplicate error lines, which is noisy though the exit status remains correct.
- scripts/check_integration_pr_readiness.py:59-73 | severity=medium | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m2_5, x-ai_grok-4_20]
  PROBLEM: `gh` lookup failures are all collapsed to `None`, so the caller cannot distinguish missing issues from transient API/auth failures.
  WHY: A transient GitHub API flake turns the readiness check into a hard failure instead of a distinguishable retryable state.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:8605-8627 | severity=medium | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m2_5, x-ai_grok-4_20]
  PROBLEM: The dedup signature state file is rewritten without locking or a retry-safe atomic update path.
  WHY: Concurrent poll ticks can race the write and leave stale or corrupted dedup state, causing repeated alerts or missed notifications.
- scripts/lint_pr_body_auto_close.py:114-128 | severity=medium | confidence=5
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, minimax_minimax-m2_5, moonshotai_kimi-k2_5, x-ai_grok-4_20]
  PROBLEM: `LintViolation.format()` says “On merge this would auto-close the tracking issue” even though the workflow only checks the PR body.
  WHY: The wording implies title/commit-message coverage that the check does not provide, which misleads users about the remaining bypass path.
=== END CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===

=== FINDINGS FROM deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro ===
- scripts/lint_pr_body_auto_close.py:76 | severity=high | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: The regex still accepts an optional colon between the auto-close keyword and the issue reference.
  WHY: GitHub does not treat colon-form keywords as auto-close triggers, so the required CI check will block clean PRs that mention prose like `Closes: #2734`.
- tests/test_lint_pr_body_auto_close.py:74,104 | severity=medium | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: The test cases `("Closes: #100", "Closes", None, 100)` and `("Resolves: https://github.com/owner/repo/issues/9", "Resolves", "owner/repo", 9)` encode colon-form references as valid positive matches.
  WHY: They pin the overmatching behavior, so the test suite will not catch the intended regex tightening.
- scripts/lint_pr_body_auto_close.py:commit b542c257 | severity=medium | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: The commit message describes three specific fixes that the actual diff does not implement.
  WHY: It creates a false audit trail that suggests the PR-title bypass and colon-overmatch gaps are closed when they remain open.
- scripts/lint_pr_body_auto_close.py:248-256 | severity=low | confidence=2
  PROBLEM: When `label_lookup()` returns `None`, the cache stores `None` and later duplicate references append another identical lookup error.
  WHY: The cache prevents re-fetching but does not prevent duplicate error entries, so a transient gh failure becomes repeated log noise.
- tests/test_lint_pr_body_auto_close.py:68-115 | severity=medium | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: No negative test coverage exists for colon-form references.
  WHY: A future regex change that re-introduces colon-form matching would go undetected.
- scripts/lint_pr_body_auto_close.py:116-121 | severity=medium | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The violation message says "On merge this would auto-close the tracking issue" even though the required workflow only validates the PR body, not the PR title or commit messages.
  WHY: The absolute wording implies the workflow covers all auto-close paths, but the PR-title bypass remains open.
=== END FINDINGS FROM deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro ===

=== FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m2_5 ===
- scripts/lint_pr_body_auto_close.py:74-81 | severity=high | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: The regex pattern uses `\s*:?\s+` which allows an optional colon between the auto-close keyword and issue reference.
  WHY: This causes the regex to match "Closes: #N" even though GitHub does not treat colon-form keywords as auto-close triggers.
- tests/test_lint_pr_body_auto_close.py:74 | severity=medium | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: The test case `("Closes: #100", "Closes", None, 100)` treats the colon-separated form as a valid match.
  WHY: GitHub does not auto-close on "Closes: #N" form, so this encodes the wrong behavior.
- .github/workflows/lint-pr-body-auto-close.yml:53-62 | severity=high | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: The workflow only writes the PR body to the lint input file and does not include the PR title.
  WHY: On squash merge, GitHub combines title and body into the commit message, so a title keyword can still auto-close the issue while the check passes.
- scripts/check_integration_pr_readiness.py:69-73 | severity=medium | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: All `gh` command failures collapse to returning `None`, so the caller cannot distinguish missing issues from transient API problems or authentication failure.
  WHY: A transient GitHub API flake can turn the readiness check into a hard failure and require manual re-runs.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:8625-8627 | severity=medium | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: The `jq` rewrite of `STATE_FILE` for `external_finalize_partial_alert_sig` uses no flock, no atomic replace retry loop, and can race.
  WHY: Multiple concurrent poll ticks can leave a stale or corrupted signature and cause repeated warnings or lost dedup state.
=== END FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m2_5 ===
